text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Social Democratic party and the labour movement are up in arms over numerous scandals the abuse of taxpayers' money, the retiring information director of labour movement ABF says.

- Opposition to Culture Minister Marita Ulvskog's plans to move four Stockholm museums to Gothenburg has met fierce opposition from all parliamentary parties, and the proposal is likely to be scrapped.

- Police are likely to keep the Malmo and Hasslarp headquarters of the Hells' Angels bikers' gang closed for some time after the recent escalation of a pan-Nordic conflict between the Hell's Angels and the rival Bandidos gang.
- Injuries sustained at work cost society as much as 60 billion crowns per year, new figures show.

- European Commission director Allan Larsson says high unemployment in Europe is partly the result of politicians' long-held belief that it is cheaper to let people claim benefits than to train them for a new job.

- Attempts to sabotage Stockholm's Metro system have increased dramatically. Concrete blocks and other objects left on the rails are a serious threat to safety, and there is a real threat of a serious accident, officials say.

- Exports from Sweden to Germany, the country's largest export market, fell by 11 percent during the first half of the year. The stronger crown was not the only cause of the shortfall -- Swedish companies are not active enough on the German market, the paper said.

- Sverker Martin-Lof, president of forestry group SCA, says he does not understand those who say the group should be split up. The company does not plan any new acquisitions, but says it will concentrate on improving profitability.
- Telecoms group Ericsson has doubled its annual turnover in Denmark to two billion crowns in the space of just a few years.

- Christopher Lewinton, chairman of Britain's TI group, says his company's plans to acquire Swedish polymer group Forsheda is an "acquisition for growth," adding that Forsheda is a good company with good products.
